Contributing to thermify

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thanks for your interest in thermify! Contributions of every size are welcome: a typo fix, a clearer example, a bug report with a reproducible case, a new index or a validation against station data.

Ways to help

  • Report a bug with the Bug report template. A minimal reproducible example (a few lines of R that anyone can run) is the most useful thing you can give.
  • Suggest a feature with the Feature request template: say what you want to compute, for which crop or region, and which reference describes the method.
  • Ask a question in Discussions rather than in an issue.
  • Pick an issue labelled good first issue: they are small, self-contained and described step by step.

Development set-up

# install.packages(c("devtools", "testthat", "roxygen2"))
# clone https://github.com/djwillichile/thermify and open the project, then:
devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)
devtools::load_all()
devtools::test()

Optional test groups (network reads, the tempify backend, reference implementations) are described in docs/TESTING.md.

Making a change

  1. Open an issue first for anything larger than a small fix, so we can agree on the approach.
  2. Create a branch from main named code/<short-description>.
  3. Keep the change focused. Add or update tests in tests/testthat/ for any change in behaviour: every method in thermify is tested against closed forms, numerical integration or an independent implementation, and new code should follow that standard.
  4. Document functions with roxygen2 (#' comments) and run devtools::document().
  5. Add a bullet to the top section of NEWS.md.
  6. Run devtools::check() and make sure it passes without errors or warnings.
  7. Open a pull request. The CI runs R CMD check on Linux, Windows and macOS plus the full test battery; please make sure it is green.

Style

  • Code follows the tidyverse style guide: two-space indent, snake_case, lines up to 80 characters.
  • Functions from other packages are called with pkg::fun() inside the package.
  • Methods cite their original publication in @references.
  • Messages, documentation and code are written in English; issues and discussions may be in English or Spanish.

Scientific changes

thermify computes quantities that people use to make decisions. A change that alters numerical results must explain why, cite the source of the method and include a test that reproduces a published or independently computed value.

Code of conduct

Please note that this project is released with a Contributor Code of Conduct. By participating you agree to abide by its terms.
